A Great Place to Grow
Spring Grove School in Wye, Kent, is a Nursery and Prep school for children aged 2 – 11, set in 14 acres of beautiful grounds and widely known for combining a warm, family ethos with academic achievement. It is located between Ashford and Canterbury, close to the high-speed train into London for commuting parents. Spring Grove offers a broad and balanced education that allows children to fully develop their curiosity, creativity and confidence. With consistently good Kent Test results, and excellent links with local independent schools, Spring Grove is a great place for your child to grow – come and see for yourself!

pageCache.pageTitle: Spring Grove Parent-School Partnership - Spring Grove
pageCache.text:
Parent-School Partnership
From Nursery through to Prep 6, parent partnership with school is vital to ensure the best outcomes for all the children at Spring Grove School. We always welcome parental support and involvement. This page tells you about some of the ways we promote partnership between parents and the school from the moment your child starts at Spring Grove.
Every Friday we hold a Family Assembly, to which all parents from both Nursery and School are warmly invited. This is a chance to meet other parents over a cup of coffee, and to watch your children perform and receive their certificates and awards.
How do parents get involved in school life? There are many occasions when parents are invited into the school and given a chance to get involved with school life. For example some parents help with art projects, others volunteer to go on trips, or help out with drama productions. If a parent has a particular expertise we love to invite them into school to speak to the children about it. And at Christmas, our parent elves are always welcome helpers at the Christmas lunch.
How often do you have Parent Meetings? Parents are invited in for formal meetings with their child’s teachers in the Autumn and Spring terms. These meetings are an opportunity for parents to discuss their child’s wellbeing, academic progress and all-round development with their teachers. Parents also receive a full written report during the Summer term which covers their child’s attainment, attitude to learning and key strengths demonstrated over the year, as well as aspects for development.
Can I speak to my child’s teacher at other times? Yes – as a parent you are always welcome to arrange a meeting with your child’s teachers at a mutually convenient time at any point in the school year.
How do I become a member of the Friends of Spring Grove? Everyone at Spring Grove is automatically a member of the Friends of Spring Grove – go to the Friends of Spring Grove page to find out more.
What is the role of the Parent Forum? The Spring Grove Parent Forum is a welcoming, structured environment where parents can share views, discuss school-wide matters, and contribute positively to the school community. It plays an important role in the partnership between parents and the school.
Each year group in the school is represented by up to two parents to ensure a diverse range of perspectives, and all parents are invited to suggest discussion topics for the meetings. Parent Forum meetings have covered a wide range of topics including sport, clubs, academic reports, smartphones and uniform. The Parent Forum is as an important means of communication and dialogue, and we are grateful to those parents who take the time to gather information and attend the termly meetings.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spring Grove Inspection Reports - Spring Grove
pageCache.text:
Inspection Reports
When was Spring Grove’s most recent inspection? In March 2026, Spring Grove School was inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), the body appointed by the Department for Education to oversee independent private schools in England.
Following three days of an extremely thorough inspection of all aspects of the school, we are delighted that the inspectors agreed the standards relating to leadership, quality of education, wellbeing, safeguarding and contribution to society at Spring Grove were all met.
What is the new ISI inspection framework? Since Spring Grove’s previous inspection in 2023, when the school was rated ‘excellent’ for both the quality of the pupils’ academic and other achievements, and for personal development, the ISI Inspection framework has been updated. Under the new framework, schools are no longer awarded graded judgements (such as ‘excellent’ or ‘good’). Instead, the new reports use more general evaluations, with findings and supporting evidence given in five key areas:
The new ISI framework places pupil wellbeing firmly at the heart of its evaluation: ‘Pupil wellbeing, as defined by the statute, is holistic and not a separate measure. Therefore, evidence of pupil wellbeing is found in all aspects of school life.’
leadership, management and governance;
quality of education, training and recreation;
physical and mental health and emotional wellbeing;
safeguarding.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spring Grove Wraparound Care & Clubs - Spring Grove
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care & Clubs
What time does before-school care start in the morning at Spring Grove? We offer before school care from 7.30am for all children from Nursery to Prep 6 in the term time, and in Nursery Holiday Club.
What time does after-school care close in the evening at Spring Grove? During term time after school care finishes at 6pm for all children from Nursery to Prep 6. In the school holidays, Nursery Holiday Club closes at 4.30pm.
Term-time wraparound
Breakfast Club (in the Sunley Hall/ Nursery for all EYFS Children)
Creche (in the Nursery classroom/garden)
SG Extra, including tea (in the Nursery classroom/garden)
Creche and SG Extra must be booked by 9.30am latest on the required day via the SchoolsBuddy app.
Who can go to after-school clubs at Spring Grove? The Clubs Programme is for children from Reception to Prep 6.
What time are after-school clubs at Spring Grove? Clubs take place after the end of the school day, starting at 3.30pm or 4.30pm depending on year group and the day of the week. Each club lasts for one hour.
Is there a charge for after-school clubs? Yes, there is a termly fee per club for school clubs. Spring Grove also hosts some clubs run by external companies which are charged directly by the provider (for example, Engineering Club and Cookery Club).
How do I book after-school clubs? Clubs bookings are released before the beginning of each term, and are bookable via the SchoolsBuddy app. Please contact the School Office for more information office@springgroveschool.co.uk.
Our Clubs change from term to term and may include:

Science Club – encourages curiosity and creativity.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spring Grove Music Scholarships at Spring Grove - Spring Grove
pageCache.text:
Music is an important part of everyday life at Spring Grove School, where we recognise the huge benefits that participation in all of the performing arts (including drama and dance) can bring to children. Finding the discipline and determination to learn how to play an instrument, overcoming your fear on stage, or having the confidence to speak to a hall full of people – all of these are life skills that extend far beyond school. The school’s strong performing arts tradition also means that SG leavers are frequently awarded music and drama scholarships to local independent schools.
Who is eligible for a Music Scholarship at Spring Grove? Pupils who are in current Years 2, 3 and 4 are invited to apply for scholarships starting in September 2027. Applications are open both to new pupils to the school and to existing Spring Grove School pupils.
What standard does my child need to be at to apply for a Music Scholarship? Candidates are expected to be at minimum Grade 2 (Associated Board/Trinity) level in their chosen instrument, or voice, to apply for a Music Scholarship.
My child plays the guitar – are they eligible to apply for a Music Scholarship? Absolutely! We encourage children to play as wide a variety of instruments as possible. However children holding a Music Scholarship at Spring Grove will be expected to learn an orchestral instrument (strings/woodwind/brass) from Year 3 onwards. This can be in addition to their first study instrument or voice.
How do you assess children for Music Scholarships? Scholarship assessments will be held in the Spring term 2027. External candidates may be invited in at other times if appropriate. Children will be asked to prepare a piece (or pieces) on their chosen instrument(s), or voice, for an assessment with Spring Grove School’s Director of Music.
All external candidates will be invited in for the whole day, which will also include an informal assessment of their academic ability. We aim to make this taster/assessment day as relaxed as possible and we hope that it will be a fun and positive experience for the children.
What commitments do Music Scholars have at Spring Grove? All children holding a Music Scholarship will be expected to contribute fully to the musical life of the school, taking leading roles in school musical events and promoting the enjoyment of music among the Spring Grove community.
What percentage fee reduction does the school offer for Music Scholarships? Information about the level of fee reductions, and other useful information can be found in the Scholarship Awards policy .
How do I apply for a Music Scholarship for my child? Simply complete the form below, and we will be in touch with further information.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spring Grove Spring Grove and King's Canterbury in partnership - Spring Grove
pageCache.text:
Spring Grove School and The King’s School Canterbury are delighted to announce a new partnership beginning in September 2026.
Built on a long-standing relationship between the two schools, the partnership reflects a shared commitment to providing an outstanding education, exceptional pastoral care and opportunities that allow every pupil to flourish. Both schools will retain their own identity, leadership and ethos, while working together to enhance opportunities for pupils, staff and families through greater collaboration and shared experiences.
The partnership also marks the creation of The King’s School Canterbury Education Group, reflecting the ambition of both schools to remain forward-thinking while continuing to value their rich history and traditions.
Together, Spring Grove and The King’s School Canterbury look forward to an exciting future and the opportunities this partnership will bring for children and young people in the years ahead.
The brochure and video below will tell you more about this exciting new partnership.
FAQs
While each school has its own distinct character and traditions, King’s and Spring Grove share a deep commitment to the same fundamental purpose: providing an outstanding education for children and young people in Kent and beyond.
Both schools are guided by closely aligned values. We believe in the importance of intellectual curiosity, strong pastoral care, and an education that nurtures the whole child. We also share a belief that schools thrive when they work together, drawing on collective experience, supporting one another, and continually seeking to improve what we offer to our pupils and families.
This partnership is therefore not about changing what makes each school special. Spring Grove will remain proudly Spring Grove, and King’s will remain proudly King’s. Rather, it is about bringing two strong schools into closer partnership so that, together, we can build an even more vibrant, resilient and inspiring educational community for the generations of children who will follow.
We are aiming for the merger to take place on 31st August 2026, ahead of the new academic year. This is when Spring Grove School will join the King’s School Canterbury Education Group.
The partnership between King’s and Spring Grove will create exciting new opportunities for pupils at both schools. Pupils will benefit from the sharing of expertise between teachers, as colleagues collaborate on curriculum development, pedagogy and best practice. This will strengthen teaching and learning across both schools and ensure that pupils continue to receive the highest standards of education in the classroom.
Beyond the classroom, the partnership will also create opportunities to enrich the co-curricular life of both schools. Pupils will benefit from an expanded range of activities in areas such as sport, music, drama, academic enrichment and outdoor education. There will also be opportunities for pupils to take part in shared events and initiatives that broaden their experiences and allow them to learn from one another.
The relationship between the schools will also create natural opportunities for older pupils at King’s to mentor and support younger pupils at Spring Grove, fostering leadership, confidence and a strong sense of community.
This collaboration will develop gradually and thoughtfully, with the benefits for pupils growing as the partnership matures. Over time, pupils at both schools will gain access to a richer range of experiences, opportunities and expertise while each school retains the character and environment that make it special.
The partnership will not affect fees at either King’s or Spring Grove. Fees will continue to be set for each school individually, reflecting the needs and provision of each school.
As with all independent schools, fees are reviewed periodically to ensure that the schools can continue to provide the highest quality of education, invest in facilities and support their pupils and staff.
No. Spring Grove will continue to operate as it does now. There are no plans to change the school’s name, uniform, or the structure of the school day.
Spring Grove will continue to be led by its own Head, senior leadership team and local governors, who will make decisions about the life of the school in the same way as they do now. If changes such as a new uniform were ever considered in the future, they would come from Spring Grove’s leadership and would be discussed with parents in the usual way.
The same applies at King’s: decisions about the school will continue to be made by its own leadership and governors.
No. There will be no automatic transfer or guaranteed places introduced as part of the partnership. Admissions to King’s will continue to follow the same criteria and processes as they do now.
Spring Grove has a long and successful tradition of preparing pupils for entry to a wide range of senior schools, and that will continue. Families will remain free to choose the school that is right for their child, and Spring Grove will continue to support pupils in applying to a variety of leading senior schools.
The closer relationship between the schools may strengthen the pathway for those pupils who wish to apply to King’s, but there will be no change to admissions standards or expectations.
Absolutely not. Spring Grove is a thriving and successful school, and there are no plans for it to close.
The purpose of the partnership is to support both schools in continuing to flourish as strong, self-sustaining communities within a wider charitable foundation. At a time when the prep school sector faces increasing pressures, bringing the schools into closer partnership strengthens their long-term resilience while preserving the distinctive character and independence that have made each school successful.
The intention is therefore not to change what makes Spring Grove special, but to ensure that it continues to thrive for many years to come.
The partnership will create valuable opportunities for colleagues in both teaching and non-teaching roles at King’s and Spring Grove to work more closely together. Staff will be able to share ideas, exchange expertise and learn from one another, strengthening practice across both schools.
Both schools place a strong emphasis on continuing professional development, and being part of the same family of schools will broaden opportunities for collaboration, mentoring and professional learning. Colleagues will be able to explore pedagogy together, share best practice and develop their skills through a wider professional network.
Over time, this will help create a vibrant professional community in which staff support one another, grow in their roles and continue to deliver the highest standards of education for pupils.
Overall, we are committed to a process that develops an effective Group strategy over the next few years, while supporting each school to be the best version of itself within its local context.
Yes. Both King’s and Spring Grove are strong and successful schools, and this partnership is being formed from a position of confidence rather than necessity.
Spring Grove is a thriving school: it is well run and financially secure, with strong demand from families looking ahead to future admissions. King’s likewise continues to be a flourishing and ambitious school community.
The decision to come together has therefore been driven by educational opportunity rather than financial need. Governors at both schools believe that by working in closer partnership they can build on the strengths that already exist in each community and create even greater opportunities for pupils and staff.
As with any partnership, being part of a wider family of schools brings long-term resilience and stability. The motivation for this partnership is to build on the strengths of both schools and create even greater opportunities for the years ahead.
In legal terms, Spring Grove will merge with the King’s School Canterbury charitable foundation. This means the schools will ultimately sit within the same charitable organisation and share a single employer.
However, the intention is to create a partnership between two schools that will continue to operate with their own character and approach. Being part of the same foundation will allow the schools to align strategically and collaborate where this is beneficial, while continuing to run their educational programmes and day-to-day operations as they do now.
King’s and Spring Grove have enjoyed a close and positive relationship for many years. The idea of a more formal partnership emerged naturally through conversations between the schools last year. Neither school was actively seeking a partnership, but the strength of the existing relationship, together with a shared ethos and educational vision, made it something worth exploring further.
Over recent months, senior leaders and Governors at both schools have given the proposal careful consideration, weighing the potential opportunities and challenges. It is only following this thorough process that both schools have concluded that a partnership would be in the best interests of their communities.
Above all, both schools are confident that working together will create meaningful long-term benefits for pupils while preserving the distinctive character of each school.
King’s and Spring Grove are different in size, history and educational setting, and that difference is one of the strengths of the partnership.
Spring Grove is a highly regarded prep school where academic rigour and wellbeing go hand in hand. It has a vibrant community and an excellent record of preparing children for a wide range of senior schools. King’s brings the strengths of a larger and historic senior school, with its long tradition of academic excellence and a rich co-curricular life.
What matters most is that the schools share a common vision for education and a strong set of underlying values. Both place great importance on intellectual curiosity, excellent pastoral care and a broad education that develops the whole child.
The intention is not to make the schools the same, but to allow two distinct schools to work together in ways that build on their respective strengths.
No. This partnership has been carefully designed so that both schools continue to flourish as distinct and successful communities.
While Spring Grove will join the King’s School Canterbury Education Group, Spring Grove and King’s will each retain their own Department for Education registration, Head, senior leadership team and local governance, with responsibility for the day-to-day leadership and development of their school. There will also be reciprocal representation on each other’s governing body, helping to ensure that the interests, perspective and character of both schools are clearly understood and reflected as the partnership develops.
Both schools are thriving and well led. The intention is not to change what makes either school successful, but to strengthen both communities through collaboration and shared opportunity, while preserving the independence and distinctive character of each school.
Both King’s and Spring Grove value the expertise and commitment of their staff, and colleagues at both schools will continue to play an important role as the partnership develops.
As part of the process, staff currently employed by Spring Grove will transfer to King’s as their employer under TUPE regulations. This is the standard legal framework used when organisations come together and ensures that existing contracts transfer with the same terms and conditions.
In practice, this means that colleagues will continue in their roles as they do now, with the same protections and employment terms, while becoming part of a wider community of staff across the two schools.
Spring Grove has been very well run and, as a result, has built up healthy financial reserves over time. These reserves provide security for the school and allow it to plan confidently for the future. King’s likewise maintains appropriate reserves to protect the school from financial uncertainty.
As part of the partnership, it has been agreed that the reserves built up by Spring Grove will remain available for the benefit of the school. Rather than being pooled, they will continue to support Spring Grove and may be used to invest in the school’s future, for example through capital projects or other developments.
Each school will continue to plan and manage its own finances, setting budgets that support its educational priorities and long-term development.
Being part of the same charitable foundation will provide a stronger platform for investment where this will benefit the school and its pupils. Proposals for significant investment will be considered carefully, with clear educational and financial planning behind them.
As with any well-run school, investment decisions will be made prudently and with a long-term view.
Nothing will change in the short term. Both schools will continue to operate as they do now, with the same leadership, staff, routines and school life.
Pupils will continue their education in the same environment, with the same teachers and pastoral structures that families already know. The distinctive character and day-to-day experience of each school will remain unchanged.
Over time, the partnership will create opportunities for closer collaboration between the schools, but this will develop gradually and thoughtfully, with the aim of enhancing what each school already does well.
There are no immediate plans to expand the group beyond King’s and Spring Grove. Any future developments would be considered carefully and as part of the long-term strategy of the King’s School Canterbury Education Group.
Our immediate focus is on building a strong and successful partnership between the two schools. Over time, it is possible that other schools with a similar vision for education and shared v

pageCache.text:
Governors
The Governors at Spring Grove bring a diverse range of expertise, knowledge and interests from many walks of life. Working as a whole team and within smaller sub-committees, they ensure the school continues to provide an excellent all-round education for all of our pupils. The Spring Grove Governors also plan the school’s future direction in conjunction with the Head and the Strategic Leadership Team (SLT), ensuring that the school continues to develop and move forward to be ‘the best it can be’.
The Governors are ultimately accountable for the performance of the school to parents and the wider community. They appoint the Head and the Bursar (in consultation with the Head), make decisions on the school’s budget, fee levels and staffing, decide how the school can encourage pupil and staff development and make sure the school provides for all its current and prospective pupils, whatever their need.
Our Governors meet regularly and are at the core of what we do, working successfully with our Head and the SLT.
The Chair of Governors, Mr Andrew Martin, can be contacted by phoning or emailing Vicky Jones, the Clerk to the Governors, who is also the school’s Bursar (01233 812337 / bursar@springgroveschool.co.uk).
The address and telephone number of the Governing Body’s registered office is: Spring Grove School, Harville Road, Wye, Ashford, Kent TN25 5EZ. Telephone: 01233 812337.
The Governing Body:
Prior to starting his career in agriculture, Andrew spent 3 years working in the French Alps for a hotel management company. He has managed a number of farms in southern England before returning to the family farm in 1996. He has farmed in the area for over 30 years and is now an Agricultural Consultant for an international firm of land agents and is director of a company that gives arable farming advice throughout the whole of southern England. Andrew also runs a local business that maintains, restores and refurbishes classic cars. He has two children, both of whom are former pupils of Spring Grove. When not working or with the family he enjoys cycling and skiing.
Sarah is a civil servant and a parent at Spring Grove. Sarah has held a variety of governor roles at three local primary schools and is the governor responsible for Early Years. As well as being Vice Chair of the Governors, Sarah is also Chair of the Academic Committee.
Lydia has 25 years of experience working in education. Starting her career in the primary sector, she then spent a few years in early years before going back to primary focusing on supporting students with additional needs. In 2019 she ventured into secondary education and started working at Wye School where she soon became SENCO. After 5 years in post, she decided to try something completely different and is now training to become a financial adviser.
Tanya Lee joined the SMT of the King’s School, Canterbury as the Pastoral Deputy Head in September 2011. Her career has been very much along the pastoral route as she was a Housemistress at both St Mary’s, Wantage and Wycombe Abbey School and then Head of Boarding at Headington School in Oxford. In addition to her current role she is an inspector with the ISI and a tutor for the BSA on the Roehampton Housemasters training courses. Tanya has returned to her Kent roots having grown up in Broadstairs and Walmer and is delighted to be back in the area. She joined the governing body of Spring Grove in the Spring of 2012 and is the nominated Safeguarding Governor.
Alexia is a solicitor at a global leading law firm in the Ci­ty, specialising in professional liabili­ty and insurance law. Alexia is also a parent at Spring Grove and joined the gov­erning body in Octob­er 2022.
Elizabeth is a Barrister specialising in Family Law. She also sits as a Deputy District Judge and Arbitrator. Elizabeth is a parent at Spring Grove and was appointed as a Governor in 2025.
A freelance IT Consultant, Dominic is Chair of Governors at a local primary school and is a former parent at Spring Grove. He is Chair of the Finance Committee.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
The Prep curriculum covers Years 3 to 6 (Key Stage 2), when the children consolidate their KS1 learning and continue to develop their independence as they prepare for Year 6 and life beyond Spring Grove at their senior schools.
At Spring Grove we believe in offering a rich, broad and balanced curriculum for all our pupils. We try hard to make links in learning across lessons and across subjects where appropriate. At times we create focus weeks, where we come off-timetable to explore ideas, activities and knowledge linked to particular themes.
We believe that young learners thrive on the chance to perform, communicating their learning and their developing confidence through assemblies and other productions, meaning that time is dedicated to these activities throughout the year.
Curious and collaborative
Our values are embedded in all that we do at SG. Throughout our Prep curriculum children are encouraged to be curious, to work collaboratively to solve problems together and to ask the big questions. Having a Growth Mindset is key and we encourage all our children to be ‘can-do’ people. Craftsmanship is also important: we teach our children to show pride in what they do, learning from mistakes. Making mistakes is an essential part of learning and an indicator that our children are always pushing themselves to try more challenging and adventurous tasks.
We use topics to inspire the children and make their learning fun. Responsive Teaching is key for us; teachers use formative assessment every day to inform their teaching and planning. Teachers provide immediate, corrective, verbal feedback to support each child’s progress. All Prep children at Spring Grove have their own school Chromebook for use in the classroom.
Children in the Prep enjoy regular Forest School sessions, swimming lessons in the Summer and Autumn terms, and a range of trips linked to the curriculum. Each child also has their own Chromebook for use in the classroom. We offer specialist Sport, Music, Dance, Art and French teaching, as well as an increased use of specialist teachers for other subjects as children move towards Prep 6, taking advantage of the in-depth and expert knowledge of our staff and preparing the pupils for their transition to secondary education.
Following mastery pedagogy, teachers review previous learning, know what each pupil can do and have an understanding about each pupil’s way of thinking.
Through the Prep curriculum we concentrate on building an understanding of the basic processes of Maths; we value the repetition in our learning of tables. We learn to develop confidence and understanding in Maths through games, practical activities and challenges. We allow the children the opportunity to research and explore mathematical problems and we teach them how to set down their work on paper, or on their Chromebooks, with clarity and accuracy.
We ensure that all of our children are prepared for the Maths challenges they will face in their next schools when they leave Prep 6.
“The value of English in the curriculum? What can I say? Without English, nothing, and without good English, nothing very well.” Anne Fine
English is fundamental to every aspect of the curriculum, and at Spring Grove children are given the skills needed to develop their confidence in communicating effectively. English is taught with rigour and enthusiasm throughout the school, and we aim to develop each individual pupil’s full potential in reading, writing, and speaking and listening.
Our English curriculum is aligned to the National Curriculum but goes far beyond these national expectations. Our planning puts texts at the heart of what we do, helping the children to become expert readers and writers as well as confident speakers and careful listeners. English lessons enable children to share a wide variety of books and on-screen texts from all genres. Children are assessed regularly to ensure a smooth progression in skills and concepts, including application of spellings, punctuation and grammar. Spring Grove pupils thrive on being able to demonstrate their dramatic skills and knowledge of stories, both fictional and true, in their many performances to a range of audiences.
Pupils study an engaging and lively range of topics throughout their study of English, including poetry, Shakespeare, writing for different purposes, non-fiction texts and classic as well as picture books, contemporary novels and short stories. Drama is taught alongside English, with pupils assisted in their applications for Drama Scholarships should they wish to pursue this further.
There is a well-stocked school library as well as regular events to help inspire the children further, such as author visits, book fairs, World Book Day events, reading challenges, and more!
Teaching is carefully sequenced, progressing learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spring Grove From Nursery to Reception - Spring Grove
pageCache.text:
From Nursery to Reception
How do we prepare children for the move into Reception class? We know that moving to full-time school is a big change for many children, and we plan our activities and timetable carefully in Giraffes to allow the children to build up their confidence and stamina as they near the end of their pre-school year.
all help our Giraffes children to be ready for the next step up, either into the Reception class at Spring Grove or another school.
Do all Nursery children stay at Spring Grove? No, we don’t have capacity for all Nursery children to stay on into Reception at Spring Grove, so some children always move to other schools in the local area. However, the group of children who stay on into the Reception class at Spring Grove School have a wonderfully soft transition in a familiar setting, with teachers they will already have met and got to know while at Nursery.
Wherever your child is going for their Reception year we aim to make the transition as easy as possible.
If you would like to find out more about the Reception class at Spring Grove you can book a personal tour any day during term time – click the link below.
Parents of Nursery children are encouraged to register early for the Reception class if they are interested in their child staying on at Spring Grove School, as places quickly fill up. Children who have not been at Spring Grove Nursery are very welcome in our Reception class (subject to places being available), and we make every effort to ensure that the transition is as smooth as possible for all new school starters whether they have been at home, with a childminder or attended another setting.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spring Grove Creative Arts - Spring Grove
pageCache.text:
Creative Arts
The Creative Arts at Spring Grove School stimulate curiosity and imagination within our children. The Art department is located in a quirky attic room where children are able to express themselves freely. The areas of focus are: drawing, textiles, painting, printing, sculpture, collage and digital art. Prep children are taught by a specialist teacher, whilst Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 have art lessons in their classrooms with their form teachers.
For every child in the school, teaching and learning within the art curriculum aims:
Children are introduced to a wide range of tools and techniques to enable them to record from observation, experience and imagination. We improve children’s awareness of visual and tactile elements of art and design, and allow them to develop their understanding of colour, form, texture and pattern. Through a variety of art projects, we teach children about the differences and similarities of artists and craftspeople from different cultures. Sometimes art topics are linked to other curriculum areas, sometimes we study a style of a particular artist, and sometimes we let our art topic stand alone!
to grow as a reflective, thinking artist.
Celebrating the Creative Arts
Artsmark
In January 2024 Spring Grove was awarded Artsmark Gold – a quality standard for schools awarded by Arts Council England.
Spring Grove embarked on its Artsmark journey in 2020, and since then has clearly demonstrated how it goes about fulfilling its mission for the arts to: ‘offer our children unique opportunities to express themselves and engage in their learning in a variety of ways.’
The broad, creative curriculum offered at Spring Grove School helps all of its pupils to have opportunities to develop their knowledge and talents and to become curious and creative learners – skills that will remain with them for life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spring Grove Performing Arts - Spring Grove
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts
Music, drama and dance are important parts of everyday life at Spring Grove School, where we recognise the huge benefits that participation in the performing arts can bring to all children. Finding the discipline and determination to learn how to play an instrument, overcoming your fear on stage, or having the confidence to speak to a hall full of people – all of these are life skills that extend far beyond school. The school’s strong performing arts tradition also means that SG leavers are frequently awarded music and drama scholarships to local independent schools.
Performing Arts in the Curriculum
Music
School music plays an important role in the intellectual development of a child, and many studies have shown its positive impact. It has the unique ability to excite or relax, stimulate or calm, invigorate or soothe, or simply to entertain. It has the power to directly and positively impact the wellbeing of a child, both instantaneously and over a period of time. It is a very important part of each child’s experience at Spring Grove.
Children begin their musical journey when they start at SG, beginning with Nursery music sessions. From Reception class onwards, all children have an hour long weekly lesson. In addition, they can join in with choirs, orchestras and small ensembles to complement the work of the classroom and further enrich their musical world.
Lessons are taught by our Director of Music, Mr Dray-D’Anna, a music specialist whose instrumental skills include the keyboards, Celtic harp, mandolin, guitar, accordion and electric bass. All lessons take place in the Bill Jones Music Room, which incorporates a large teaching and orchestral space as well as two smaller teaching/practice rooms. The music curriculum is broad-based with a strong practical approach, allowing children to sing and to play many different types of instruments. As they discover the language of music, theoretical knowledge and notation is introduced, the relevance of which is considerably enhanced by the child’s practical musicianship skills. To fit everything into context, the history of music and musical cultures is taught with a focus on listening to music from all eras.
The ultimate aim is to promote a well rounded, exciting musical world with the tactile satisfaction of playing instruments combined with enough theoretical knowledge to be able to fully appreciate and create music. Of the many stated benefits of a musical education, above all, we believe that it should be fun!
Dance and Drama
Dance is an integral part of the curriculum at Spring Grove. From Baby Ballet classes for our youngest children to the elaborate dance routines devised by our older pupils, we recognise the benefits that expression through movement brings to all children. Drama is timetabled into the curriculum for children from Prep 3 upwards, and all children have the opportunity to appear on stage whether in on of the many shows held every year, or in class assembly presentations – a highlight of the week on Friday mornings. Our visiting LAMDA teacher also offers weekly lessons in the dramatic arts, instilling confidence and skill for public speaking and performance.
Visiting Music Teachers
Mr Dray-D’Anna leads a team of Visiting Music Teachers who go out of their way to nurture the talents of the children at Spring Grove. A large number of children from Years 1 to 6 have individual music lessons on a wide variety of instruments, and voice, and we frequently celebrate music exam success in our Friday Family assemblies.
Opportunities to Perform
Children at Spring Grove are fortunate to have a wide range of opportunities to perform in shows, concerts, showcases and assemblies. All children in the school are encouraged to take part.
The school has a tradition of high-quality theatrical performances ranging from the Nativity productions for Giraffes/Reception and Years 1 and 2 at Christmas, to the musicals performed by Preps 3 and 4 at the end of the Spring term, and for Preps 5 and 6 at the end of the Summer term. Recent productions have included ‘The Wizard of Oz’, ‘Boogie Woogie Nativity’ and ‘Joseph and his Technicolour Dreamcoat’.
Informal Concerts are regular termly events that give all children, whatever their level of playing, an opportunity to perform. The School Prom concert is a highlight of the summer, showcasing the best of the musical, dance and performance talent in the school.
Spring Grove is often asked to provide musicians for local events such as the Service of Remembrance at Wye Church, and music for the residents at a local Care Home. At Christmas our school choir is honoured to perform in Canterbury Cathedral at the Princess of Wales’s Regiment Carol Service.

Parent Reviews
As a school, how do we check in with our parents? Parent-school partnership is at the heart of everything we do at Spring Grove, and parents are always welcome to check in with staff, either in person or by email.
Every term the Strategic Leadership Team meets with parents at the Parent Forum, set up to discuss all aspects of school life. The Parent Forum plays an important role in the partnership between parents and the school.
What do parents say about Spring Grove? “We are so grateful for the brilliant support and encouragement – from her first introduction to Mrs Jaggard (and lovely welcome card) to the encouraging, inspiring and patient teaching she enjoys each and every day.”
“Spring Grove meets all of our wish list for our son, and some – the warm familial environment, the beautiful setting and facilities, the breadth of activities and resources available and the all round creative, physical and academic focus. We toured a number of nurseries and schools and Spring Grove stood out head and shoulders above the rest. It feels like a place that is an absolute privilege for your child to attend.”
“I discovered Spring Grove on Google and was instantly impressed. I felt this was the place for my children when browsing through your website. You come across as a welcoming and inclusive school and I believe my two will benefit from the family atmosphere. The emphasis on good manners and conduct along with the caring, nurturing and encouraging approach particularly appeals to me. The outdoors aspect is an unexpected bonus.”
“Our son has blossomed at the school since he started as a 2-year-old. He loves it there and the teachers. His communication skills are brilliant, we listen in astonishment with all the new phrases he comes out with. His school lunch looks so nice; I often wonder if I could pop down for lunch, all hot and freshly cooked.”
“We found Spring Grove after a web search of primary schools within easy access of the fast train service into London. It looked like a small, friendly school with high standards without too much academic pressure. When I contacted the school they were quick to reply and provide information and seemed friendly and open to engaging with parents.”
“Spring Grove stood out as a perfect choice for our son, not only for the enthusiasm and nurturing atmosphere that came through the website, but also the school’s commitment to make its children well-rounded individuals, thriving on encouragement.”
“We chose Spring Grove because we really liked the emphasis on being outdoors. I was also impressed by the Head’s emphasis on finding each child’s talents and nurturing them.”
“We chose Teddies because the staff were all so friendly and the children seemed happy and relaxed.”
“We wanted to take the time to write and thank the Spring Grove staff for all the energy and effort you all put into life at SG. We never find there is enough time to stop and express our gratitude during the busy working week but wanted to do so now, at Christmas. Our children have been at SG for six months and what an amazing time they have had so far! Moving the children has been the best decision we have ever made and the difference in them is immense. We have loved watching their confidence grow through all the praise and encouragement. Every single day, they are positively pushed out of their comfort zone, performing in an assembly or trying something new to eat. Everyone at SG has made us feel so welcome and we feel lucky to be part of the school. Thank you!”
“We arranged to view the Nursery and was so impressed and felt so comfortable and at home, we decided on the spot to send both sons!”
“We are so grateful for the brilliant support and encouragement – from her first introduction to Mrs Jaggard (and lovely welcome card) to the encouraging, inspiring and patient teaching she enjoys each and every day.”
Come and see for yourself what our parents love about Spring Grove! You can book a personal tour any time during term time, or if a weekend visit is easier, register for one of our Saturday morning Open Mornings held in October and March each year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Spring Grove School History - Spring Grove
pageCache.text:
School History
Spring Grove boasts a long and fascinating history before it became the happy, family school of today. The school is set in 14 acres of beautiful Kent countryside and is based in a magnificent Tudor/Stuart house, completed in the late 17th century.
Early History
The house was built in the mid-16th century (around 1550), and was originally called William Wells Hall. In 1674 it was refaced and extended by Dr Thomas Brett. By then the house was called Spring Grove. It was subsequently lived in by generations of the same Brett family. In the mid-19th century Spring Grove was home to Charles Jenyns, a businessman who moved from London to Wye to take advantage of the new, fast train service from rural Kent into the City: perhaps an early example of regular commuting into town. Jenyns was also an amateur painter and his watercolour of Wye, which includes a passing train, hangs in Wye Church.
Writers at Spring Grove
During the 20th century Spring Grove was home to the writer Joseph Conrad for 6 months in 1919, and a little over a 100 years before that, Jane Austen may well have been a visitor when she was staying at nearby Godmersham House, owned by her brother Edward.
School History
Spring Grove School owes its origins to Cynthia Christopherson who decided to create a school for her son and a few friends. The school opened its doors on 15 September 1967 with 12 pupils, led by Mrs Rosa Cobb, who was the Headmistress for the first ten years of the school’s life. In 1984, Mr and Mrs Christopherson sold the school to Niall Washington-Jones. After Mrs Cobb’s retirement, Mr Washington-Jones guided the school and established its reputation as a family school with a homely atmosphere and emphasis on good manners. In 2003 a group of parents bought the school and set it up as a charitable trust administered by a Board of Governors. Craig Gibbs served as Headmaster from 2004 to 2007.
From 2008 to 2020 Bill Jones was Headmaster and, together with his wife Hilary, strengthened Spring Grove’s reputation as a school that provides a first-class education for primary-age pupils, preparing them for their next schools. Bill was succeeded as Head in Autumn 2020 by Therésa Jaggard, who led the school through the difficult times of the Covid-19 pandemic. In 2023, Spring Grove was awarded ‘Excellent’ in all aspects by the Independent Schools Inspectorate, followed by another very successful ISI inspection three years later in 2026.
SG50
SG50 was launched in 2017 to celebrate 50 years of Spring Grove School. In September 2017, two of the school’s first pupils, David Christopherson and Roger Pitt, visited and spoke to the children about how the school helped them to forge their life-long friendship, in a wonderful illustration of the powerful part the school can play in the lives of its pupils. In May 2018, a whole-school photograph included Springgrovians and Huw Jones, son of Bill and Hilary Jones and Scotland Rugby International, who also opened the school’s new Sports Pavilion.
Partnership with The King’s School Canterbury
From September 2026, Spring Grove will start an exciting new chapter in its history when the school enters into partnership with The King’s School Canterbury.
